Natural_Language: This part applies to acquiring information and communication technology (ICT), and supplies and services that use ICT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_001_a_1_a: This part applies to acquiring ICT; P_39_001_a_1_b: This part applies to acquiring supplies and services that use ICT
Validation_Notes: Mandatory applicability statement. Both ICT directly and supplies/services using ICT are within scope. Conjunction captures that both categories are covered simultaneously.

Natural_Language: This part emphasizes strategies that promote faster acquisition and secure deployment of technology that is new or emerging.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_001_a_2_a: This part emphasizes strategies promoting faster acquisition of new or emerging technology; P_39_001_a_2_b: This part emphasizes strategies promoting secure deployment of new or emerging technology
Validation_Notes: Policy emphasis statement. Both faster acquisition and secure deployment are emphasized in parallel. Declarative 'will'-type statement describing Part purpose.

Natural_Language: Applicability and emphasis of Part 39 regarding ICT acquisition.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_001_a: Part 39 applies to ICT acquisition and emphasizes speed and security strategies
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition joining applicability scope with policy emphasis. Both subsections define scope and direction of Part 39.

Natural_Language: This part does not apply to acquiring information technology for national security systems; as defined in 40 U.S.C. 11103.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_001_b_a: Acquisition is for information technology for national security systems as defined in 40 U.S.C. 11103; P_39_001_b_b: Part 39 does not apply
Validation_Notes: Exclusion clause. If the acquisition is for national security systems (as defined by external statute), then Part 39 does not apply. Material implication correctly captures the conditional exclusion. HIGH-RISK flagged because Impl Rule 15 is used; direction of implication is clear here (national security status triggers exclusion).

Natural_Language: Applicability of Part 39 -- Acquisition of Information and Communication Technology.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_001: Part 39 applicability consists of scope provisions and national security exclusion
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 39.001. Combines positive applicability scope with national security exclusion.

Natural_Language: Before entering into an information technology contract, agencies should analyze risks, benefits, and costs. Reasonable risk taking is appropriate as long as risks are controlled and mitigated.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_101_a_a: Before entering into an IT contract, agencies analyze risks, benefits, and costs; P_39_101_a_b: Reasonable risk taking is appropriate; P_39_101_a_c: Risks are controlled and mitigated
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' for risk analysis makes first atomic recommended, not mandatory. Second sentence uses conditional: risk taking is appropriate only when risks are controlled. HIGH-RISK flagged for implication. Real-world: agencies are advised to do risk analysis and may accept risk if controlled.

Natural_Language: Both contracting and program office officials are responsible for assessing, monitoring and controlling risk throughout the acquisition process.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_101_b_a: Contracting officials are responsible for assessing, monitoring, and controlling risk throughout the acquisition process; P_39_101_b_b: Program office officials are responsible for assessing, monitoring, and controlling risk throughout the acquisition process
Validation_Notes: Mandatory shared responsibility. 'Both...are responsible' establishes dual obligation. Conjunction captures that each group independently holds responsibility.

Natural_Language: Management of risk in IT acquisitions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_101: Risk management requirements for IT contracts
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Contains advisory (should) and mandatory components. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW because parent inherits advisory status from 39.101(a).

Natural_Language: Agencies should use modular contracting (i.e., use one or more contracts to acquire information technology systems in successive, interoperable increments) to acquire major systems of information technology, to the maximum extent possible (see 41 U.S.C. 2308). Agencies may also use modular contracting to acquire non-major systems of information technology.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_a_a: Agencies use modular contracting to acquire major IT systems to the maximum extent possible; P_39_102_a_b: Agencies use modular contracting to acquire non-major IT systems
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' for major systems plus permissive 'may' for non-major systems. Major systems have strong advisory push ('to the maximum extent possible'). Non-major systems use tautology to represent discretionary authority. External statutory reference to 41 U.S.C. 2308.

Natural_Language: When acquiring an information technology system (i.e., either a major system or non-major system), it may be divided into several smaller increments (see 41 U.S.C. 2308(c)) that meet criteria in (b)(1) through (b)(4).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_b_a: Agency is acquiring an IT system; P_39_102_b_b: IT system is divided into several smaller increments meeting criteria in (b)(1)-(b)(4)
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may' creates discretionary authority to divide IT system into increments. Condition (acquiring IT system) triggers discretion (may or may not divide). Tautology in consequent represents unrestricted choice. Subsection criteria (b)(1)-(b)(4) apply only if division is chosen.

Natural_Language: Are easier to manage individually than would be possible in one comprehensive acquisition.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_b_1: Increments are easier to manage individually than in one comprehensive acquisition
Validation_Notes: Criterion for increments under modular contracting. Atomic statement describing a quality that increments must possess. Applies conditionally when agency elects to divide per 39.102(b).

Natural_Language: Address complex information technology objectives incrementally to enhance the likelihood of achieving workable systems or solutions for attainment of those objectives.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_b_2: Increments address complex IT objectives incrementally to enhance likelihood of achieving workable systems or solutions
Validation_Notes: Criterion for increments. Single atomic describing purpose of incremental approach. Conditionally applicable per 39.102(b).

Natural_Language: Provide for delivery, implementation, and testing of workable systems or solutions in discrete increments, each of which comprises a system or solution that is not dependent on any subsequent increment in order to perform its principal functions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_b_3_a: Each increment provides for delivery, implementation, and testing of workable systems or solutions; P_39_102_b_3_b: Each increment is not dependent on any subsequent increment to perform its principal functions
Validation_Notes: Dual criterion: increments must both deliver workable systems AND be independently functional. Key interoperability requirement -- each increment stands alone.

Natural_Language: Provide an opportunity for subsequent increments to take advantage of any evolution in technology or needs that occur during implementation and use of the earlier increments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_b_4: Subsequent increments can take advantage of technology evolution or needs changes occurring during earlier increments
Validation_Notes: Criterion for increments. Ensures flexibility for technology evolution. Single atomic requirement.

Natural_Language: To promote compatibility, each increment should comply with common or commercially acceptable information technology standards when available and appropriate, and be compatible with other (including earlier and later) increments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_c_a: Each increment complies with common or commercially acceptable IT standards when available and appropriate; P_39_102_c_b: Each increment is compatible with other increments (including earlier and later)
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' makes this recommended, not mandatory. Both standards compliance and inter-increment compatibility are recommended. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW due to advisory nature.

Natural_Language: Award a contract for an increment within 180 days after the date on which the solicitation is issued. If an award cannot be made within 180 days, agencies should consider cancelling the solicitation in accordance with 14.209 or 15.206(e).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_d_1_a: Contract for an increment is awarded within 180 days after solicitation issuance; P_39_102_d_1_b: Award cannot be made within 180 days; P_39_102_d_1_c: Agency considers cancelling the solicitation in accordance with 14.209 or 15.206(e)
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' governs both the 180-day target and the cancellation consideration. If award cannot be made within 180 days, agencies should consider cancellation per 14.209 or 15.206(e). External dependencies on Parts 14 and 15. HIGH-RISK flagged for implication.

Natural_Language: Schedule deliveries under the contract to occur within 18 months after the solicitation was issued.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_d_2: Deliveries under the contract are scheduled within 18 months after solicitation issuance
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' (inherited from parent 39.102(d)) makes this recommended. Single atomic timeline requirement.

Natural_Language: When using modular contracting, agencies should, to the maximum extent possible, meet the requirements in (d)(1) and (d)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102_d_a: Agency is using modular contracting; P_39_102_d_b: Requirements in (d)(1) and (d)(2) are met to maximum extent possible
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Advisory 'should' with conditional trigger (when using modular contracting). Both timeline requirements apply together. HIGH-RISK flagged for implication.

Natural_Language: Modular contracting requirements and criteria for IT system acquisitions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_102: Modular contracting encompasses usage guidance, increment criteria, compatibility standards, and timeline requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 39.102. Mix of advisory (should) and permissive (may) provisions. PENDING_REVIEW because parent inherits advisory status.

Natural_Language: When acquiring information technology services, solicitations should not describe any minimum experience or educational requirements for proposed contractor personnel, unless the contracting officer determines that the needs of the agency cannot be met without that requirement or require using other than a performance-based acquisition (see subpart 37.6).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_103_a: Agency is acquiring IT services; P_39_103_b: Solicitation does not describe minimum experience or educational requirements for contractor personnel; P_39_103_c: CO determines agency needs cannot be met without the requirement; P_39_103_d: CO determines agency needs require using other than performance-based acquisition
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex nested conditional with advisory 'should not'. When acquiring IT services, unless one of two exceptions applies (needs cannot be met OR non-performance-based required), solicitations should avoid minimum experience/education requirements. The 'unless' creates a negated condition triggering the default rule. Advisory nature (should) means not strictly mandatory. HIGH-RISK for nested implications.

Natural_Language: Cannot be met without that requirement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_103_a_exc: Agency needs cannot be met without minimum experience or educational requirements
Validation_Notes: First exception to the general rule in 39.103. Atomic condition that, if true, permits minimum experience/education requirements in solicitations.

Natural_Language: Require using other than a performance-based acquisition (see subpart 37.6).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_103_b_exc: Agency needs require using other than a performance-based acquisition
Validation_Notes: Second exception to the general rule in 39.103. Atomic condition referencing subpart 37.6 for performance-based acquisition standards.

Natural_Language: ICT accessibility standards comprising scope, policy, applicability, exceptions, and exemptions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104: ICT accessibility standards consist of scope (39.104-1), policy (39.104-2), applicability (39.104-3), exceptions (39.104-4), and exemptions (39.104-5)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 39.104. All five subsections collectively define the ICT accessibility framework.

Natural_Language: This section implements section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. 794d), and the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board's (U.S. Access Board) ICT accessibility standards at 36 CFR 1194.1.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_1_a_a: Section 39.104 implements section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. 794d); P_39_104_1_a_b: Section 39.104 implements the U.S. Access Board ICT accessibility standards at 36 CFR 1194.1
Validation_Notes: Declarative implementation statement. Both statutory authority (Section 508) and regulatory standards (36 CFR 1194.1) are implemented. External legal references.

Natural_Language: For further information on section 508 visit http://www.section508.gov.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_1_b: Further information on section 508 is available at section508.gov
Validation_Notes: Informational reference. No regulatory requirement or obligation created. Atomic statement.

Natural_Language: Scope of ICT accessibility standards section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_1: Scope encompasses statutory implementation and information reference
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for 39.104-1. Both implementation authority and information pointer.

Natural_Language: When acquiring ICT, agencies must ensure that Federal employees with disabilities have access to and use of information and data that is comparable to the access and use by Federal employees who are not individuals with disabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_2_a_a: Agency is acquiring ICT; P_39_104_2_a_b: Federal employees with disabilities have comparable access to and use of information and data
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must ensure' with conditional trigger (when acquiring ICT). Comparable access standard is the requirement. HIGH-RISK flagged for implication; direction is clear (ICT acquisition triggers accessibility obligation).

Natural_Language: When acquiring ICT, agencies must ensure that members of the public with disabilities seeking information or services from an agency have access to and use of information and data that is comparable to the access to and use of information and data by members of the public who are not individuals with disabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_2_b_a: Agency is acquiring ICT; P_39_104_2_b_b: Members of the public with disabilities have comparable access to and use of information and data
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must ensure' with conditional trigger. Parallel to (a) but extends to public-facing access. Same implication structure.

Natural_Language: When acquiring ICT, agencies must ensure comparable access for both Federal employees and members of the public with disabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_2: ICT accessibility policy requires comparable access for employees and public
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Both employee and public accessibility obligations apply simultaneously. Inherits PENDING_REVIEW from children using HIGH-RISK rules.

Natural_Language: Unless an exception at 39.104-4 or an exemption at 39.104-5 applies, acquisitions for ICT supplies and services must meet the applicable ICT accessibility standards at 36 CFR 1194.1.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_3_a_a: Exception at 39.104-4 applies; P_39_104_3_a_b: Exemption at 39.104-5 applies; P_39_104_3_a_c: Acquisitions for ICT supplies and services meet applicable ICT accessibility standards at 36 CFR 1194.1
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' with 'unless' creating negated condition. Default rule: comply with 36 CFR 1194.1. Exception (39.104-4) or exemption (39.104-5) removes obligation. The 'unless' inverts: when neither exception nor exemption applies, compliance is mandatory. HIGH-RISK for nested implication with negation.

Natural_Language: When acquiring commercial products and commercial services, an agency must comply with those ICT accessibility standards that can be met with supplies or services that are available in the commercial marketplace and that best address the agency's needs, but see 39.104-5(a)(3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_3_b_a: Agency is acquiring commercial products and commercial services; P_39_104_3_b_b: Agency complies with ICT accessibility standards meetable with commercially available supplies/services that best address agency needs
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' with conditional trigger (commercial acquisition). Compliance is scoped to what is commercially available. Cross-reference to 39.104-5(a)(3) for nonavailability exemption. HIGH-RISK for implication.

Natural_Language: Complies with an earlier standard issued according to section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. 794d), which is set forth in Appendix D to 36 CFR 1194.1.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_3_c_1: Legacy ICT component complies with an earlier section 508 standard set forth in Appendix D to 36 CFR 1194.1
Validation_Notes: First condition for legacy ICT exemption from current standards. Atomic requirement referencing earlier standards.

Natural_Language: Has not been altered (i.e., a change that affects interoperability, the user interface, or access to information or data) after January 18, 2018.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_3_c_2: Legacy ICT component has not been altered after January 18, 2018
Validation_Notes: Second condition for legacy ICT exemption. 'Altered' is specifically defined as changes affecting interoperability, user interface, or data access. Date threshold is January 18, 2018.

Natural_Language: Any component or portion of existing ICT (i.e., ICT that was procured, maintained, or used on or before January 18, 2018) is not required to comply with the current ICT accessibility standards if it meets both conditions in (c)(1) and (c)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_3_c_a: ICT component was procured, maintained, or used on or before January 18, 2018; P_39_104_3_c_b: Component is not required to comply with current ICT accessibility standards
Validation_Notes: Legacy ICT exemption. Three conjunctive conditions (pre-2018 ICT + earlier standard compliance + no alteration) must all be met to trigger exemption from current standards. HIGH-RISK for implication with triple conjunction in antecedent.

Natural_Language: When altering any component or portion of existing ICT, after January 18, 2018, the component or portion must be modified to conform to the current ICT accessibility standards in 36 CFR 1194.1.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_3_d_a: Agency is altering a component or portion of existing ICT after January 18, 2018; P_39_104_3_d_b: The component or portion is modified to conform to current ICT accessibility standards in 36 CFR 1194.1
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' with conditional trigger (alteration of legacy ICT after cutoff date). Any alteration triggers current standards compliance. Logically consistent with 39.104-3(c) -- alteration removes the legacy exemption.

Natural_Language: Applicability of ICT accessibility standards including general rule, commercial products, legacy ICT, and alterations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_3: ICT accessibility applicability covers general, commercial, legacy, and alteration scenarios
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for 39.104-3. All four applicability provisions operate together. Inherits PENDING_REVIEW from children.

Natural_Language: ICT operated by agencies as part of a national security system, as defined by 40 U.S.C. 11103(a).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_4_a_1: ICT is operated as part of a national security system as defined by 40 U.S.C. 11103(a)
Validation_Notes: Exception: national security system ICT is exempt from 39.104-2 requirements. Material implication with negation of parent obligation. External statutory reference.

Natural_Language: ICT acquired by a contractor incidental to a contract, i.e., for in-house use by the contractor to perform the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_4_a_2: ICT is acquired by a contractor incidental to a contract for in-house use to perform the contract
Validation_Notes: Exception: incidental contractor ICT (in-house use) is exempt from 39.104-2 requirements. Narrow definition -- must be for contractor's own use to perform the contract.

Natural_Language: The portions of ICT that are operable parts (i.e., hardware-based user controls for activating, deactivating, or adjusting ICT) or status indicators, and that are located in spaces frequented only by service personnel for maintenance, repair, or occasional monitoring of equipment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_4_a_3_a: ICT portions are operable parts or status indicators; P_39_104_4_a_3_b: ICT portions are located in spaces frequented only by service personnel for maintenance, repair, or monitoring
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Exception: maintenance/monitoring space ICT. Two conjunctive conditions must both be met (operable parts/status indicators AND restricted-access location). HIGH-RISK for implication with conjunction in antecedent.

Natural_Language: The requirements in 39.104-2 do not apply to acquisitions for national security systems, incidental contract items, or maintenance/monitoring spaces.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_4_a: Three categories of acquisitions are excepted from 39.104-2 requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent for exception categories. Disjunction because any single exception is sufficient to remove the 39.104-2 obligation. Meeting any one of (a)(1), (a)(2), or (a)(3) triggers the exception.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must receive, as a part of the requirements documentation, written confirmation from the requiring activity that an exception, in accordance with paragraph (a)(1), (2), or (3) of this section, applies to the ICT supply or service (see 7.105(b)(5)(iv)). This documentation must be maintained in the contract file.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_4_b_a: CO receives written confirmation from requiring activity that an exception under (a)(1), (2), or (3) applies; P_39_104_4_b_b: Documentation is maintained in the contract file
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' for both receiving documentation and maintaining it. Dual obligation on the CO. External cross-reference to 7.105(b)(5)(iv).

Natural_Language: Exceptions to ICT accessibility requirements including categories and documentation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_4: Exception framework consists of three exception categories and documentation requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent for 39.104-4. Both the exception categories and the documentation requirement are part of the exception framework.

Natural_Language: When an agency determines the acquisition of ICT conforming with all the applicable ICT accessibility standards would impose an undue burden on the agency, compliance with the ICT accessibility standards is only required to the extent that it would not impose an undue burden. In determining whether conformance to one or more ICT accessibility standards would impose an undue burden, an agency must consider the extent to which conformance would impose significant difficulty or expense considering the agency resources available to the program or component for which the ICT supply or service is being procured.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_a_1_a: Agency determines full ICT accessibility compliance would impose undue burden; P_39_104_5_a_1_b: Compliance is required only to the extent it does not impose undue burden; P_39_104_5_a_1_c: Agency considers extent of significant difficulty or expense relative to available resources
Validation_Notes: Undue burden exemption. Determination of undue burden triggers partial compliance requirement and mandatory resource consideration. Does not eliminate all compliance -- only reduces to extent not burdensome. HIGH-RISK for implication.

Natural_Language: When an agency determines that acquisition of ICT that conforms with all applicable ICT accessibility standards would result in a fundamental alteration in the nature of the ICT, such acquisition is required to conform only to the extent that conformance will not fundamentally alter the nature of the ICT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_a_2_a: Agency determines full accessibility conformance would fundamentally alter the nature of the ICT; P_39_104_5_a_2_b: Acquisition conforms only to extent conformance does not fundamentally alter ICT nature
Validation_Notes: Fundamental alteration exemption. Parallel structure to undue burden. Partial compliance still required -- exemption only covers the portion that would fundamentally alter ICT. HIGH-RISK for implication.

Natural_Language: Where there are no commercial products and commercial services that fully conform to the ICT accessibility standards, the agency must procure the supplies or service available in the commercial marketplace that best meets the ICT accessibility standards consistent with the agency's needs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_a_3_a: No commercial products/services fully conform to ICT accessibility standards; P_39_104_5_a_3_b: Agency procures commercially available supplies/services that best meet ICT accessibility standards consistent with agency needs
Validation_Notes: Commercial nonavailability exemption. Mandatory 'must' -- when no fully conforming commercial option exists, agency must procure best available. Not discretionary. HIGH-RISK for implication.

Natural_Language: An agency may grant an exemption for undue burden, fundamental alteration, or nonavailability of conforming commercial products and services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_a: Three exemption categories are available
Validation_Notes: Parent for exemption categories. Permissive 'may grant' creates discretionary authority. Disjunction because any single exemption basis is sufficient. PENDING_REVIEW due to permissive modal.

Natural_Language: An agency must provide individuals with disabilities access to and use of information and data by an alternative means to meet the identified needs when an exemption in paragraphs (a)(1), (2), or (3) of this section applies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_b_a: An exemption under (a)(1), (a)(2), or (a)(3) applies; P_39_104_5_b_b: Agency provides individuals with disabilities access by alternative means
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' -- when any exemption is granted, alternative access is required. Key safeguard ensuring exemptions do not eliminate accessibility entirely. HIGH-RISK for implication.

Natural_Language: A determination of undue burden must address why and to what extent compliance with applicable ICT accessibility standards constitutes an undue burden.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_c_1: Undue burden determination addresses why and to what extent compliance constitutes undue burden
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation content for undue burden exemption. Single atomic requirement specifying what the determination must contain.

Natural_Language: A determination of fundamental alteration must address the extent to which compliance with the applicable ICT accessibility standards would fundamentally alter the nature of the ICT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_c_2: Fundamental alteration determination addresses extent to which compliance would alter ICT nature
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation content for fundamental alteration exemption. Single atomic requirement.

Natural_Language: A description of the market research performed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_c_3_i: Determination includes a description of the market research performed
Validation_Notes: First required element of nonavailability determination. Atomic documentation requirement.

Natural_Language: A listing of the requirements that cannot be met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_c_3_ii: Determination includes a listing of requirements that cannot be met
Validation_Notes: Second required element of nonavailability determination. Atomic documentation requirement.

Natural_Language: The rationale for determining that the ICT to be procured best meets the ICT accessibility standards in 36 CFR 1194.1, consistent with the agency's needs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_c_3_iii: Determination includes rationale for why procured ICT best meets standards consistent with agency needs
Validation_Notes: Third required element of nonavailability determination. Atomic documentation requirement.

Natural_Language: A determination of commercial products and commercial services nonavailability must include a description of market research, listing of unmet requirements, and rationale for procurement decision.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_c_3: Nonavailability determination includes market research description, unmet requirements listing, and procurement rationale
Validation_Notes: Parent for nonavailability determination contents. All three elements are mandatory (must include). Conjunction captures that all are required.

Natural_Language: When an exemption applies, the contracting officer must obtain, as part of the requirements documentation, a written determination from the requiring activity explaining the basis for the exemption. Maintain this documentation in the contract file.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5_c_a: An exemption under (a)(1), (a)(2), or (a)(3) applies; P_39_104_5_c_b: CO obtains written determination from requiring activity explaining basis for exemption; P_39_104_5_c_c: Documentation is maintained in the contract file
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation requirement triggered by exemption. CO must both obtain the determination AND maintain it in the file. HIGH-RISK for implication. Parallel structure to 39.104-4(b) for exceptions.

Natural_Language: Exemptions from ICT accessibility standards including categories, alternative access requirement, and documentation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_104_5: Exemption framework covers categories, alternative access, and documentation
Validation_Notes: Parent for 39.104-5. All three components (exemption types, alternative access mandate, documentation requirements) operate together as the exemption framework. Inherits PENDING_REVIEW.

Natural_Language: Confirming an exception (see 39.104-4) or determining an exemption (see 39.104-5) is not required before awarding of an indefinite-quantity contract, except for requirements that the initial award is to satisfy.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_201_a_a: Acquisition is an indefinite-quantity contract award; P_39_201_a_b: Exception/exemption confirmation is not required before award; P_39_201_a_c: Requirements are for initial award satisfaction
Validation_Notes: Timing exception for IDQ contracts. Exception/exemption documentation can be deferred to task order level, except where initial award includes specific requirements that need accessibility compliance. Complex conditional with exception-to-the-exception. HIGH-RISK for implication.

Natural_Language: The contract must identify which supplies and services the contractor indicates as compliant and show where to find full details of compliance (e.g., a contractor may provide a link to a vendor's website identifying supplies or services that are fully compliant with ICT accessibility standards).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_201_b_a: Contract identifies which supplies and services the contractor indicates as compliant; P_39_201_b_b: Contract shows where to find full details of compliance
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' for contract content. Dual obligation: identify compliant items AND provide details/reference. Parenthetical example (vendor website link) is illustrative, not prescriptive.

Natural_Language: ICT accessibility standards for indefinite-quantity contracts covering timing of exceptions/exemptions and contract content requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_201: IDQ contract accessibility rules cover exception timing and compliance identification
Validation_Notes: Parent for 39.201. Both timing and content provisions apply. Inherits PENDING_REVIEW from (a).

Natural_Language: When issuing a task order or delivery order under an indefinite-quantity contract, the requiring activity and ordering activity must ensure compliance with the ICT accessibility standards. For a noncompliant ICT item, the requiring activity must document an exception (see 39.104-4) or exemption (see 39.104-5).
Atomic_Propositions: P_39_301_a: Task order or delivery order is being issued under an IDQ contract; P_39_301_b: Requiring activity and ordering activity ensure compliance with ICT accessibility standards; P_39_301_c: ICT item is noncompliant; P_39_301_d: Requiring activity documents an exception per 39.104-4 or exemption per 39.104-5
Validation_Notes: Mandatory 'must' with nested conditional. When issuing orders: (1) ensure accessibility compliance AND (2) if noncompliant, document exception or exemption. Note: source text references 39.104-5 for both exception and exemption, which appears to be a typo -- exception should reference 39.104-4. Flagged for review. HIGH-RISK for nested implications.
